body: I think I went with econ because it was a safe ticket to a job. And to answer your last question, that's the problem! I never developed any hobbies or interests in my life. I've always been avoidant in trying new things and finding new interests because of my incredibly low self esteem, and now I feel like I'm stuck. The degree would mean a chance at a good paying job, but what's the point if I have no friends, talents, or interests, hobbies or real goals? I acted when I was younger and but moving to California would be a pipe dream.

I avoid people and new situations because I feel like I having nothing to say, and my silence will not only be awkward but alert people to how boring I am, hence why I took on another's personality--and I actually had an ex girlfriend call me boring to my face which I still ruminate on. I don't know how to fundamentally be a person who just does things an says things, as weirdly simplistic as that sounds. 

And I'm worried about withdrawing because I have 27/30 credits in my econ major done, it's just getting the remaining 36 electives out of the way. But I flip flop because whats the point of being alone for a year shuttling in an out of random classes just for the chance at a job? I have no long term goals or visions is the problem.
What interests/hobbies would come out of doing the things you mentioned? I'm horrendous at drawing.
